title: Shared reference domes raised the joint error threshold for two harebell width contrasts in North Wales in 2021
abstract: We tested whether one set of bounded cell errors can remove two seasonal harebell flower-width contrasts that share reference domes. We used a public ozone and warming experiment in North Wales in 2021. We reproduced earlier campaign contrasts and derived their exact joint error region. The minimum cell-error allowance for both zero contrasts was 2.38%, compared with 1.54% from separate bounds. At a 2% allowance, both separate intervals contain zero, but the joint region excludes both zero values. Linear programming over the original cell errors agreed with the formula. Month omission gave joint thresholds of 1.69-3.37%. These are assumed error limits, not observed errors or confidence limits. One site, one year, selected flowering plants and one dome per treatment prevent causal or broad biological claims. This is a method extension using the same data as the earlier result, not an independent replication.

display.caption: Exact joint error region at an assumed 2% cell-error bound, and thresholds that permit both seasonal contrasts to be zero. Separate bounds form a larger rectangle.
